005package org.wpilib.opmode;
006
007import java.util.Set;
008import org.wpilib.framework.OpModeRobot;
009import org.wpilib.internal.PeriodicPriorityQueue;
010
011/**
012 * Top-level interface for opmode classes. Users should generally extend one of the abstract
013 * implementations of this interface (e.g. {@link PeriodicOpMode}) rather than directly implementing
014 * this interface.
015 *
016 * <p><b>Lifecycle</b>:
017 *
018 * <ul>
019 *   <li>constructed when opmode selected on driver station
020 *   <li>disabledPeriodic() called periodically as long as DS is disabled. Note this is not called
021 *       on a set time interval (it does not use the same time interval as periodic()). If the
022 *       opmode is selected while the DS is already enabled, disabledPeriodic() is called exactly
023 *       once, immediately after construction and before start()
024 *   <li>when DS transitions from disabled to enabled, start() is called once
025 *   <li>while DS is enabled, periodic() is called periodically at {@link OpModeRobot#getPeriod},
026 *       and additional periodic callbacks added via addPeriodic() are called periodically on their
027 *       set time intervals
028 *   <li>when DS transitions from enabled to disabled, or a different opmode is selected on the
029 *       driver station when the DS is enabled, end() is called, followed by close(); the object is
030 *       not reused
031 *   <li>if a different opmode is selected on the driver station when the DS is disabled, only
032 *       close() is called; the object is not reused
033 * </ul>
034 *
035 * <p>All lifecycle callbacks and periodic callbacks run synchronously on the same thread that
036 * invokes them. Interactions between opmodes and the robot framework do not require additional
037 * synchronization.
038 *
039 * <p>Additional callbacks can be registered by implementing {@link #getCallbacks()} to return a set
040 * of {@link PeriodicPriorityQueue.Callback} objects with custom timing. {@link PeriodicOpMode}
041 * provides a convenient implementation of this method and utility methods for adding periodic
042 * callbacks.
043 */
044public interface OpMode extends AutoCloseable {
045  /**
046   * This function is called periodically while the opmode is selected and the robot is disabled.
047   * Code that should only run once when the opmode is selected should go in the opmode constructor.
048   *
049   * <p>If the opmode is selected while the robot is already enabled, this is called exactly once,
050   * right after construction and before {@link #start()}.
051   */
052  default void disabledPeriodic() {}
053
054  /** Called once when this opmode transitions to enabled. */
055  default void start() {}
056
057  /**
058   * This function is called periodically while the opmode is enabled at the rate returned by {@link
059   * OpModeRobot#getPeriod()}.
060   */
061  default void periodic() {}
062
063  /**
064   * This function is called asynchronously when the robot disables or switches opmodes while this
065   * opmode is enabled. Implementations should stop blocking work promptly.
066   */
067  default void end() {}
068
069  /**
070   * This function is called when the opmode is no longer selected on the DS or after an enabled run
071   * ends. The object will not be reused after this is called.
072   */
073  @Override
074  default void close() {}
075
076  /**
077   * Returns a set of custom periodic callbacks to be executed while the opmode is enabled.
078   *
079   * <p>This method allows opmodes to register arbitrary periodic callbacks with custom execution
080   * intervals. The callbacks are executed by the robot framework at their scheduled times, in
081   * addition to the primary {@link #periodic()} callback.
082   *
083   * <p><b>Registration timing</b>: The callbacks returned by this method are registered with the
084   * framework immediately when the OpMode is constructed and begin executing as soon as they are
085   * registered. To restrict execution to only when the robot is enabled, callbacks should include
086   * an if (RobotState.isEnabled()) check at the beginning.
087   *
088   * @return A set of custom callbacks to execute, or an empty set if no custom callbacks are
089   *     needed. The default implementation returns an empty set.
090   */
091  default Set<PeriodicPriorityQueue.Callback> getCallbacks() {
092    return Set.of();
093  }
094}
